title: Microsoft Purview: higher auto-labeling limits for SharePoint sites and simulation, plus new reporting
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, licensing statement, limits and PowerShell controls are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. Minor corrections should extend the control paths beyond their entry points and acknowledge the checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The change increases policy scale and adds reporting visibility.
claims.quote: These enhancements expand support for larger SharePoint scopes, improve policy management flexibility, and provide richer visibility into auto-labeling activity.

claims.claim: The notice increases simulation capacity from 4 million to 20 million items.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling simulation capacity will increase from 4 million items to 20 million items.

claims.claim: The notice permits selecting up to 1,000 individual SharePoint sites when configuring policies.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to select up to 1,000 individual SharePoint sites when configuring policies.

claims.claim: The notice gives adaptive scopes a limit of 50,000 SharePoint sites per policy.
claims.quote: Adaptive scopes will support up to 50,000 SharePoint sites per policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The notice says SharePoint sites can be filtered with SiteTemplate during policy configuration.
claims.quote: SharePoint sites can be filtered using the SiteTemplate property during policy configuration.

claims.claim: The notice adds auditing and reporting summaries of SITs detected when labels are applied.
claims.quote: Audit and reporting experiences will provide additional visibility, including summaries of the Sensitive Information Types (SITs) detected when labels are applied.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice describes a new 30-day chart showing files processed each day.
claims.quote: A new 30-day processing chart will display the number of files processed each day, helping administrators monitor policy throughput and activity over time.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft says the change expands processing capacity rather than changing labeling behavior.
claims.quote: The change expands processing capacity rather than changing labeling behavior.

claims.claim: Learn documents a simulation limit of 20,000,000 matched files.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Each policy can explicitly include or exclude up to 1,000 SharePoint sites in the portal.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites

claims.claim: A SharePoint adaptive scope supports up to 50,000 sites per auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: For auto-labeling policies, a SharePoint adaptive scope supports up to 50,000 sites per policy.

claims.claim: The Labeling activity overview chart covers the last 30 days.
claims.quote: Its **Labeling activity overview** chart has separate successful and failed series for the last 30 days.

claims.claim: The Labeling activity overview chart has separate successful and failed series.
claims.quote: Its **Labeling activity overview** chart has separate successful and failed series for the last 30 days.

claims.claim: A simulation matching more than 20,000,000 files prevents turning the policy on until it is narrowed and simulation rerun.
claims.quote: If more than this number of files are matched from an auto-labeling policy, you can't turn on the policy to apply the labels. In this case, you must reconfigure the auto-labeling policy so that fewer files are matched, and rerun simulation.

claims.claim: The 20,000,000-file maximum applies only to simulation, not policies already turned on.
claims.quote: This maximum of 20,000,000 matched files applies to simulation mode only and not to an auto-labeling policy that's already turned on to apply sensitivity labels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning a policy on after simulation requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from **Ready to turn on** to **On** requires **Compliance Administrator** or **Compliance Data Administrator**.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Review pages require one of Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Information Protection Admin or Information Protection Analyst.
claims.quote:
To view the review pages, you need one of the following roles:

- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Information Protection Admin
- Information Protection Analyst

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Policies selecting administrative units must use All for SharePoint rather than Included or Excluded.
claims.quote:
For organizations that are using administrative units and selected in the policy:

    - For SharePoint, you can't use the **Included** or **Excluded** options and must use the **All** default selection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling applies labels without user interaction.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support *recommended* labeling

claims.claim: The absolute daily throughput ceiling is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant across all policies.
claims.quote: The **absolute maximum throughput** is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The daily throughput ceiling is not a guaranteed processing rate.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 auditing must be on for simulation.
claims.quote: **Auditing is turned on for Microsoft 365.** Required for simulation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published separate licensing for these scalability and reporting enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling scalability enhancements 570445 licensing meter SIT reporting new roles; read auto-labeling licensing, Purview service description sensitivity-labeling matrix, adaptive scopes and Insights. No enhancement-specific entitlement found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate meter for these enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling scalability enhancements 570445 licensing meter SIT reporting new roles; read Purview service description and auto-labeling licensing. No meter for these simulation, site-limit or policy-reporting enhancements found.

claims.claim: A different license specifically for the new SIT summaries and processing reports is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview auto-labeling enhancements Insights SIT summaries reporting licensing additional license meter roles; read Insights and Purview service description. No separate entitlement found for these policy-reporting enhancements.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not mention a charge.
claims.quote: Searched: Read the complete supplied MC1469958 notice, including rollout, impact, recommendations and compliance considerations; no price, meter or charge is mentioned.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling is not available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible when the tenant cannot support the regional functionality.
claims.quote: If your tenant can't support this functionality, the **Auto-labeling** page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Create auto-labeling policy is the portal entry point for explicit SharePoint targeting.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal ... **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**. ... Select **+ Create auto-labeling policy**.
claims.fix: The path stops at the creation wizard. Extend it to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Create auto-labeling policy > Automatically apply label only > Choose info you want this label applied to > Custom > Custom policy > Choose a label to auto-apply > Assign admin units > Choose locations where you want to apply the label > SharePoint > Included', following https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically#creating-an-auto-labeling-policy.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation $spoLocations -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications adds explicit SharePoint locations to a policy.
claims.quote: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation $spoLocations -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications

claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes opens the portal page for configuring adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > **Settings** > **Roles and scopes** > **Adaptive scopes**. ... On the **Adaptive scopes** page, select **+ Create scope**.
claims.fix: The path stops on the scope-list page. Extend it to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > Create scope > Full directory > SharePoint sites > Advanced query builder' to reach the documented SharePoint membership-query control at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes#how-to-configure-an-adaptive-scope.

claims.claim: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Name <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -SharePointAdaptiveScopes <AdaptiveScope> -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications creates a policy targeting an existing adaptive scope.
claims.quote: associate an existing SharePoint adaptive scope with the policy by using the `-SharePointAdaptiveScopes` parameter ... with New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy.

claims.claim: Creating adaptive scopes requires the Scope Manager role.
claims.quote: Any role group with the *Scope Manager* role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: The Compliance Administrator role group includes Scope Manager.
claims.quote:
The *Scope Manger* role is included in the following built-in role groups:

- Compliance Administrator

claims.claim: The auto-labeling policy commands use Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can use Security & Compliance PowerShell to create and configure auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: Associating an adaptive scope replaces static enumeration with dynamic membership without increasing the portal's explicit-site limit.
claims.quote: This doesn't increase the portal limit; instead, it replaces static site enumeration with dynamic adaptive-scope membership.

claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies reaches the portal's policy list for inventory.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**.

claims.claim: Learn advises preserving needed results before editing or rerunning simulation.
claims.quote: Before you edit an auto-labeling policy or run simulation again, export any available results that you need for later comparison.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Why it matters
claims.claim: Learn recommends simulation and review before enforcing an auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: run the policy in simulation before you turn it on to help ensure correct labeling.

claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details opens the newer policy review pages.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**. Select a policy, then select **View details** in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: The newer label-application review pages have Overview, Labeled items and Labeling failures tabs.
claims.quote: The newer review page has separate **Overview**, **Labeled items**, and **Labeling failures** tabs.

claims.claim: An Insights tab summarizes detected sensitive information types.
claims.quote: The policy details panel's **Insights** tab summarizes the sensitive information types detected in labeled files.

claims.claim: The table describes general auto-labeling targeting controls rather than switches enabling this rollout.
claims.quote: These enhancements are on by default and will be available automatically as the rollout reaches your organization.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents SiteTemplate filtering as an adaptive-scope query property for including or excluding site types.
claims.quote: you can use the indexed site property **SiteTemplate** to include or exclude specific site types.

claims.claim: No new role specific to these enhancements is described.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling scalability enhancements 570445 licensing meter SIT reporting new roles. Read auto-labeling prerequisites and review roles, Insights permissions, adaptive-scope roles and MC1469958; no enhancement-specific role found.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm that the roles you need are assigned'; 'Check whether any policy in your tenant uses administrative units'; 'Test any enlarged policy in simulation first'. The table has only explicit site selection and adaptive-scope targeting rows.
claims.fix: The role-assignment check, policy administrative-unit check and simulation step have no corresponding controls-table rows. Remove those three checklist bullets if strict checklist/table alignment is required; do not add control rows as part of this correction.
